title: Laguna Commerce — Relevance sprint: hosted API deep run
next_steps: Share SOC2/ISO security pack and KMS whitepaper
Schedule 1-week pilot start call (week of Nov 8)
Provide sample benchmark script and seed dataset
action_items: Maya Chen: Email pricing tiers & pilot SOW by 2027-10-29
Owen Patel: Share benchmark script + sample request templates by 2027-11-01
Asha Iyer (Laguna): Provide 10k query+doc sample and access to dev Pinecone sandbox by 2027-11-03
Sam Nguyen (Laguna): Confirm networking constraints (VPC/egress) by 2027-10-30
header:
Date: 2027-10-28
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Ruth Delgado (Redwood Product), Ben Torres (Laguna HO Search), Asha Iyer (Laguna ML Eng), Sam Nguyen (Laguna Platform), Priya Rao (Laguna PM), Leo Martinez (Laguna Legal)
summary: 30-40 minute hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking flow for Laguna Commerce search. Covered Redwood Console rerank tooling, Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization, and end-to-end sample benchmark. Customer concerned about latency SLAs for product search, data residency, and KMS integration. Agreed to run a 1-week pilot with 10k queries to evaluate relevance lift and cost per query.
topics: Hosted embeddings endpoint, reranker endpoint, vector DB integration patterns, Console rerank tooling, Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/kv cache/quantization), security (SOC2, KMS, VPC), SLAs & pricing, pilot scope and next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Ben Torres: Yep loud and clear.
[00:07] Maya Chen: Great, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, joining with Owen our SE and Ruth product. We're gonna walk through a hosted API demo for embeddings plus a reranker pipeline, and then talk pilot. Rough plan 30-35 min demo, 15 min Q&A.
[00:20] Asha Iyer: Sounds good. We've been struggling with product search precision — relevance drops when sparse queries hit long catalogs.
[00:25] Owen Patel: Right — so we'll show a canonical flow: Redwood embeddings endpoint -> vector DB (we'll show Pinecone/Relevance examples) -> candidate retrieval -> Redwood hosted reranker endpoint to rerank top-k. We'll highlight Console and Optimize suggestions for batch sizing and caching.
[00:40] Priya Rao: Quick ask — we have a 200ms 95th percentile latency goal for SERP, is that realistic with a reranker in the mix?
[00:48] Owen Patel: Good question; 200ms p95 is tight with a heavy reranker. We usually see 120-300ms p95 depending on model size and K. For hosted, you can get sub-200ms if you: 1) use a smaller reranker model or quantized variant, 2) keep K (candidates) at 10 or below, 3) enable prefix KV caching for frequent queries. Optimize can recommend a config sample.
[01:10] Ben Torres: When you say quantized variant, you mean Redwood provides different model variants ready-to-serve?
[01:16] Ruth Delgado: Yeah we maintain model catalog entries — client-visible variants like fp16, int8 (quantized) and tuned reranker checkpoint. Console shows perf/cost tradeoffs per variant.
[01:30] Sam Nguyen: Our platform team is picky about outbound traffic — would a hosted flow require egress to third-party vector DBs? We prefer either our in-cloud managed DB or bring-your-own inside VPC.
[01:40] Owen Patel: Hosted API can integrate either way. For the pilot we typically integrate with Pinecone or our customers' managed DB. We support private link / VPC peering patterns for Dedicated/Private but for Hosted the vector DB is often the only external piece. If Laguna requires everything inside a VPC, Redwood Private is the path. But for initial pilot we can use Pinecone or a lightweight in-cloud index so you can validate relevance quickly.
[01:58] Asha Iyer: Ok cool. Could you show the API calls?
[02:02] Maya Chen: Yep — Owen will share screen and step through a couple of curl examples and then jump into Console.
[02:08] [02:08] Owen Patel (screen): sharing screen now. First, embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-emb-large -> returns 1536-d vectors. We'll show a sample request from our dev harness.
[02:25] [02:25] Transcript glitch: 'redwood emb large' transcribed as 'redwood am large'
[02:30] Owen Patel: Then retrieval — vector DB returns top 100 candidates; we showed top-100 to illustrate candidate pool but production picks top 10 pre-rerank to keep latency low. Then we call POST /v1/rerank with query and candidate contexts, model=redwood-ranker-v2, and we return reranked ids + scores.
[02:48] Ben Torres: What's the response shape for rerank? do you return explainability features?
[02:53] Ruth Delgado: Response includes score, token-level highlights at the model level (optional), and a concise rationale string if you enable structured outputs. It's not full attention weights but we do provide snippets and tokens used for scoring. That helps debug false positives.
[03:10] Priya Rao: Do you support streaming for rerank responses? We do incremental rendering in our UI.
[03:15] Owen Patel: Rerank is typically synchronous but small payloads stream ok; streaming is more common for long-text generation. For rerank we aim for single-shot low-latency responses.
[03:26] [03:26] Ben Torres: How do you recommend we set K (candidates) given our catalog size 2M SKUs?
[03:31] Owen Patel: Usually K=10-50 balancing recall vs latency. For product search we recommend K=20 for warm start; then test K=10/20/50 in pilot and track MRR/NDCG with Redwood's eval harness. Optimize can auto-suggest K based on latency budgets and initial relevance lifts.
[03:50] Asha Iyer: And what about vector dims and index type — we currently use HNSW in Pinecone.
[03:55] Owen Patel: HNSW is fine. We lean on cosine/sim/inner-product depending on your vectorization. Embedding dimension depends on model; our catalog entry suggests 1024/1536 — use the one that gives best tradeoff in eval.
[04:10] Maya Chen: I'm going to flip to Console now; you'll see a demo workspace with a rerank pipeline.
[04:15] [04:15] Owen screens Console: shows 'Pipelines' tab, rerank playground, test prompts, tokenized highlights.
[04:25] Owen Patel: Console can run batch evals: upload query set, ground truth ids, then run variations (model variant, K, quantization). It shows P95 latency, tokens used and cost per 1k queries.
[04:40] Ben Torres: That cost metric — is it just compute or does it include vector DB cost?
[04:45] Ruth Delgado: Compute only for Redwood API. We show an estimate for vector DB egress/ingest if you provide DB type, but you'll want to map that to your Pinecone invoice.
[04:55] Priya Rao: Can Optimize auto-propose batching sizes? Our infra team wants to tune batch to maximize GPU utilization.
[05:00] Owen Patel: Yes, Optimize recommends batch sizes, whether to enable continuous batching, and cache TTLs. For embeddings workloads we sometimes enable 512 batch for offline ingestion; for real-time request-level batching e.g., 8-32 depends on latency target.
[05:16] [05:16] Transcript artifact: 'optimize' transcribed as 'opt me eyes'
[05:20] Ben Torres: Security — SOC2, KMS and data retention — what's available for hosted?
[05:25] Maya Chen: Hosted API customers get SOC2 Type II compliance, audit logs accessible in Console, and we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we can discuss envelope encryption and contract-level KMS. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[05:40] Leo Martinez: Legal question — if data is sent through hosted servers for rerank, what's the retention period and can you set retention to zero for certain flows?
[05:48] Ruth Delgado: We support configurable retention policies; we can offer contract terms for zero-retention for sensitive routes under enterprise agreements or run inference in Private for full data isolation. We'll include options in the SOW.
[06:00] Priya Rao: Great. Can you demo a quick end-to-end sample with a real product query?
[06:05] Owen Patel: Yep — I'll run a live demo. I'll query 'waterproof hiking jacket women's small' and show raw retrieval vs rerank output.
[06:12] [06:12] Owen executes pipeline: embeddings -> query vector -> Pinecone top-100 -> rerank top-10.
[06:28] Owen Patel: Raw retrieval top hits include 'lightweight windbreaker', 'rain poncho' — lots of noise. After rerank, top results reorder to 'waterproof hardshell jacket', 'women's insulated rain jacket', etc.
[06:45] Asha Iyer: Nice — that aligns better. Is that using a domain-tuned reranker?
[06:50] Ruth Delgado: demo harness used reranker-v2 with small domain-tuning on retail; we showed the tuned checkpoint to illustrate impact.
[06:58] Ben Torres: Do you have metrics for relevance lift?
[07:02] Owen Patel: In this example we moved MRR from 0.42 to 0.61 on the held-out prompt set. Console shows the NDCG and MRR deltas per run.
[07:14] Priya Rao: How much token cost did that add?
[07:18] Ruth Delgado: Reranker added approx 12 tokens per example on average and moved cost ~+$0.004 per query in this run, but that depends on model size and candidate size.
[07:30] Sam Nguyen: For our scale that's material; cost per query times queries/day matters. Could Optimize model recommend a smaller reranker that preserves lift but reduces cost?
[07:38] Owen Patel: Yes — Optimize will propose smaller variants and quantization. There is usually a pareto front: small model + K=20 can match bigger model + K=50. We'll run an automated sweep in pilot.
[07:52] [07:52] Brief crosstalk: (unintelligible)
[08:00] Ben Torres: On instrumentation — what observability signals do you provide? We need error rates, per-endpoint latency distributions, token counts, and per-route cost.
[08:07] Ruth Delgado: Console gives per-route dashboards, token-level breakdown, traces, and request-level logs. We also export traces to Datadog/Prometheus and can push events to your S3 audit bucket.
[08:19] Asha Iyer: Any rate limiting / throttling configurable per route?
[08:23] Owen Patel: Yes, per-route quotas, token-rate caps, and burst settings. For pilot we'll set a small commit and a throttled burst to avoid noisy tests hitting production limits.
[08:36] Ben Torres: Regarding private data — our product descriptions have PII in some user-generated content fields. How do you handle PII in embeddings?
[08:44] Maya Chen: embeddings are treated as derived vectors but we recommend PII removal before indexing. For enterprise customers we can agree on pre-processing rules, or run inference in your Private cluster so vectors never leave your network.
[08:58] Sam Nguyen: If we do hosted, can we bring our own KMS to encrypt data at rest?
[09:03] Ruth Delgado: For Hosted, customer-managed KMS is available as an add-on via contract; for full control, Redwood Private is recommended. We'll include options in the security docs.
[09:16] [09:16] Pause while Owen changes window.
[09:24] Owen Patel: Now I'll show Console's rerank A/B runner — you can spin two variants with traffic split and measure CTR on sample queries. Useful for smoke testing the rerank's UX changes.
[09:36] Priya Rao: We measure ML impact via both offline metrics and online click metrics — does Redwood integrate client-side telemetry?
[09:43] Ruth Delgado: We provide hooks to ingest click logs; Console correlates offline eval and online signal if you push events. We can also ingest logs via S3/BigQuery.
[09:55] Ben Torres: Let's talk pilot: what does a 1-week pilot typically look like?
[09:59] Maya Chen: Pilot scope we propose: 1) Ingest 10k products + 10k query set from Laguna, 2) Run a retrieval+rerank baseline vs Redwood reranker variants, 3) Console eval runs K sweep and quantization experiments, 4) Run small live A/B on 5% traffic if you want. We provide a deliverable: relevance report + config recommendations.
[10:20] Asha Iyer: We can provide the dataset. How quickly can you spin up test endpoints?
[10:24] Maya Chen: For hosted pilot we can provision keys and test endpoints within 48 hours after SOW. If you need VPC peering that's more like 2-3 weeks.
[10:35] Sam Nguyen: Our PCI requirements might be relevant — do you support contract-level segmentation?
[10:40] Ruth Delgado: Yes we'll coordinate with legal; certain customers go Private for PCI. We'll pass legal the compliance pack.
[10:50] [10:50] Ben Torres: Who's the technical owner on Redwood side for the pilot?
[10:53] Maya Chen: Owen will be SE lead; Ruth will support evaluation and product configs. I'm owning contract and SOW.
[11:02] Owen Patel: Back to the demo — here's a Console eval run. You can see model variants lined up, P95, token usage, cost estimates per 1k queries. Notice the quantized int8 variant shows 30% lower cost with 5% drop in MRR. That's often acceptable for constrained budgets.
[11:20] Priya Rao: Can you show how to switch the reranker variant via API without changing client code?
[11:25] Owen Patel: Yes — we support named model aliases in the API route. You update the route config or alias and it's immediate; canary rollouts available for 10/20/50% traffic splits.
[11:40] Asha Iyer: For the pilot, can we measure TTFB and per-call kv cache hit rates?
[11:46] Ruth Delgado: Yes, Console shows cache hit metrics and helps you set prefix cache TTLs. KV cache here means transformer KV cache per-session — for rerank it matters less than seq-gen, but prefix caching for embeddings reuse can reduce calls.
[12:00] [12:00] Minor transcription noise - 'kv' sometimes transcribed as 'kay vee'
[12:06] Ben Torres: Any pitfalls you've seen with cataloged commerce datasets?
[12:10] Owen Patel: Noisy titles, inconsistent attribute fields, and heavy UGC generate signal dilution. We recommend field-specific embeddings (title-only, title+attrs) and ensembled scoring — reranker helps combine signals.
[12:26] Priya Rao: On vector DB cost — sometimes HNSW memory spikes during large batch reindexing. Should we expect any coordination there?
[12:34] Owen Patel: Yes coordinate ingestion windows. For pilot small datasets are fine. For production we advise staging index updates and rolling rebuilds.
[12:46] Ben Torres: I saw mention of 'autobatching' in docs — how does that interact with strict 95th latency budgets?
[12:52] Ruth Delgado: autobatching tries to improve throughput by combining requests. If you have a strict latency SLO, you can set a max batch delay or disable autobatching for that route. Optimize suggests safe parameters per SLO.
[13:08] Maya Chen: Alright, switching to cost — I'll run a quick cost calc. If you run 100k queries/day and choose reranker-v2 non-quantized with K=20, rough compute cost is $X (placeholder) — we'll send exact numbers in pricing.
[13:28] Ben Torres: Understood. Send the numbers.
[13:31] Sam Nguyen: A small ops question — will Redwood provide Terraform or IaC to create route configs?
[13:36] Owen Patel: Yes we have Terraform provider snippets and Postman/SDK examples. We'll include a sample TF module in the pilot repo.
[13:45] Asha Iyer: Any recommendations for seed prompts and negative examples to maximize eval usefulness?
[13:50] Ruth Delgado: Include representative long-tail queries, partial matches, attribute-only queries, and known hard negatives. We'll supply a template CSV.
[14:02] Ben Torres: Legal — Leo, any concerns?
[14:05] Leo Martinez: Just want to ensure data residency clauses and liability caps are in SOW. We'll review security pack first.
[14:12] Maya Chen: We'll surface both in the SOW.
[14:15] [14:15] Pause as Maya types chat link to security pack (link shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack).
[14:22] Priya Rao: Can you share the sample benchmark script now?
[14:26] Owen Patel: I'll drop the link in chat — it's a Python script using requests; it's lightweight. We'll include guidance for running with Pinecone or your DB.
[14:34] Asha Iyer: For the pilot, we want to test a smaller reranker model first to check latency. How long to retrain or tune a reranker?
[14:40] Ruth Delgado: Tuning for domain-specific retail usually takes 2-3 days for a small fine-tune if you provide labels; checkpointing and evaluation are quick. For a pure zero-shot we rely on existing tuned checkpoints.
[14:52] Ben Torres: Are there limits on candidate size you can accept in a single rerank call?
[14:58] Owen Patel: API supports up to 512 candidates but practical latency constraints mean keep it under 100; otherwise consider two-stage rerank or coarse filtering.
[15:10] Priya Rao: Can you show an example of a rerank request payload?
[15:13] Owen Patel: Sure — here's an example: POST /v1/rerank payload {"query":"...", "candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"..."}, ...], "model":"redwood-ranker-v2"}. Response is array of ids with scores.
[15:28] [15:28] Minor transcription oddity: curly braces lost in transcript.
[15:32] Ben Torres: One thought — we currently have locale-specific catalogs. Does Redwood support locale-aware reranking or locale-specific models?
[15:40] Ruth Delgado: Yes, you can route to model variants per locale and maintain locale-specific reranker checkpoints; Console supports multi-env config.
[15:50] Maya Chen: We're at ~35 minutes. Any final questions before we recap next steps?
[15:56] Asha Iyer: One last thing — do you have prebuilt adapters for Pinecone?
[16:00] Owen Patel: Yes we provide adapters and example connectors for Pinecone and Weaviate; Milvus examples are in the repo too.
[16:08] Ben Torres: Okay thanks, very helpful.
[16:12] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send pricing + SOW, security pack, benchmark script. Laguna to send sample 10k queries + product feed and confirm network constraints. SE to run initial eval and propose model/quantization configs. We'll target pilot start week of Nov 8.
[16:30] Priya Rao: That works.
[16:32] Leo Martinez: We'll review security pack.
[16:35] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links.
[16:40] Ben Torres: Thanks all.
[16:42] [16:42] Meeting ends.

Notes and artifacts referenced in chat: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack, https://github.com/redwood/inference-samples/pinecone-rerank, sample-benchmark.py (link shared in chat).
